# How to build a hero, a bento grid and a footer

*The three sections every landing page needs, each built from type scale, one accent and space.*

<sub>📖 [Read this chapter on the live site](https://frontenddesignbasics.vercel.app/docs/how-to/hero-bento-footer) for the interactive version · [← Guide contents](../README.md)</sub>

> - Hero: one huge headline, one sentence, one primary action, a texture kept behind the text.
> - Bento: the biggest cell carries the idea, one gap value everywhere.
> - Footer: name, three to five links, a real sign-off, room above it.

**Goal:** a first screen that says what this is, a grid that ranks ideas, and an ending that feels like one.

## You need

- Your type scale and tokens. See [Scales and type](../rules/scales-and-type.md).
- Optional: a shader or image for the hero texture.

```text
 HERO                     BENTO
 ┌──────────────────┐     ┌──────┬───┬───┐
 │ eyebrow          │     │ BIG  │ ▪ │ ▪ │
 │ HEADLINE, HUGE   │     │ IDEA ├───┴───┤
 │ one line, 44ch   │     │      │ story │
 │ [primary] (alt)  │     ├───┬──┴───────┤
 └──────────────────┘     │ ▪ │ action   │
                          └───┴──────────┘
 FOOTER  name · contact · source · legal · sign-off
```

## Steps

### 1. Build the hero in layers

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| Texture | A background with a subject, kept behind text |
| Headline | One huge thing per view: `clamp(3rem, 9vw, 8.5rem)`, tight leading |
| Support | One sentence, 44ch max |
| Actions | One solid button, one outline |
| Eyebrow | Small, mono, uppercase, tracked |

```tsx
<section className="relative min-h-[82svh] overflow-hidden">
  <Texture />
  <div className="relative flex min-h-[82svh] flex-col justify-between p-10">
    <p className="font-pixel text-[16px] uppercase">A field guide</p>
    <div>
      <h1 className="font-display text-[clamp(3rem,9vw,8.5rem)] leading-[0.9]">…</h1>
      <p className="mt-6 max-w-[44ch]">…</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

### 2. Reveal the headline with a mask

<img src="../img/how-to-hero-bento-footer/01-TextRevealDemo.jpg" alt="TextRevealDemo" />

<sub>▶ Interactive on the [live site](https://frontenddesignbasics.vercel.app/docs/how-to/hero-bento-footer).</sub>

Each word sits in an overflow-hidden box and slides up into view. Use an ease-out and a short stagger.

### 3. Build the bento

<img src="../img/how-to-hero-bento-footer/02-BentoDemo.jpg" alt="BentoDemo" />

<sub>▶ Interactive on the [live site](https://frontenddesignbasics.vercel.app/docs/how-to/hero-bento-footer).</sub>

```tsx
<div className="grid auto-rows-[7.5rem] gap-3 sm:grid-cols-4">
  <div className="sm:col-span-2 sm:row-span-2">The one big idea</div>
  <div>Proof</div>
  <div>Detail</div>
  <div className="sm:col-span-2">Supporting story</div>
  <div>Call to action</div>
</div>
```

The biggest cell carries the idea. The accent cell carries the action. Keep one gap value.

### 4. Finish with a real footer

- The name and one line of what it is.
- The three to five links people look for: contact, source, legal.
- A sign-off with some personality.
- Enough space above it to feel like an ending.

## Pitfalls

- **Two primary buttons.** Only one thing can be the main action.
- **A magnetic button everywhere.** Use it once, on the hero action, never on forms or nav.

<img src="../img/how-to-hero-bento-footer/03-MagneticButton.jpg" alt="MagneticButton" />

<sub>▶ Interactive on the [live site](https://frontenddesignbasics.vercel.app/docs/how-to/hero-bento-footer).</sub>

## Why it works

These sections are the rules under load: a type scale, one accent, space and motion applied to a
common job. That is why they can be reused without looking reused.
